newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa says samurai issue most competitive ever.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says samurai issue most competitive ever.

text.p: The South African Finance Department said on Tuesday that the samurai issue it had launched earlier in Tokyo was its most competitive funding ever in the markets in Libor terms.
"The issue is the longest maturity any South African issuer has in the Japanese markets and the largest transaction accomplished since the $750 million global issue in 1994," it said in a statement.
The country earlier launched a 40 billion yen, seven-year bond priced at a spread of 70 basis points of Japanese yen Libor.
The previous samurai issued in May 1995 was priced at a spread of 197 points over Libor.

"This second issue has built on the strong reputation South Africa has in the Japanese markets, and the huge success of the debut issue, which was voted IFR Samurai deal of the year in 1995," it said.
It added that the issue fulfilled all of the department's strategic borrowing objectives.
